children: Motilal Oswal expects earnings in its coverage universe to grow 11 per cent in the second half, with automobiles, financial services, metals and oil and gas supporting the outlook

Corporate earnings are expected to remain resilient in the second half of FY27, supported by healthy demand, business expansion and strong order pipelines across sectors, according to a report by Motilal Oswal Financial Services.

The brokerage expects earnings in its coverage universe to grow 11 per cent year-on-year in the second half of FY27, while the Nifty universe is projected to report 18 per cent growth. Excluding oil marketing companies (OMCs), earnings growth for the Motilal Oswal universe is estimated at 20 per cent.

The outlook follows a broad-based performance in the September quarter, with 28 sectors meeting or exceeding the brokerage's earnings expectations. Banking, financial services, insurance, metals, oil and gas, and automobiles were among the key contributors to growth.

These four broad sector groups — banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), metals, oil and gas, and automobiles — accounted for 77 per cent of incremental year-on-year earnings growth, while other sectors also contributed positively.
September Quarter Beats Estimates

Companies in Motilal Oswal's coverage universe reported a 32 per cent year-on-year increase in profit after tax (PAT) in the second quarter of FY27, exceeding the brokerage's estimate of 21 per cent. Excluding OMCs, earnings grew 30 per cent against an estimate of 24 per cent.
The Nifty 50 reported 27 per cent growth in PAT, its highest in 17 quarters, led by Reliance Industries, ONGC, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, JSW Steel and State Bank of India.

Large-cap companies in the brokerage's coverage universe recorded 31 per cent earnings growth, while mid-caps and small-caps reported growth of 22 per cent and 32 per cent, respectively, excluding OMCs.
The brokerage said 42 per cent of companies in its coverage universe exceeded its profit estimates, while 26 per cent reported a miss.
Demand Supports Sector Outlook

The automobile sector is expected to maintain its growth momentum, supported by healthy retail demand, lean dealer inventories and export growth. Two-wheeler manufacturers have indicated mid-to-high single-digit industry growth in the second half, while passenger vehicle makers are expecting high-single-digit growth.

Capital goods companies are also seeing healthy order inflows across domestic and export markets, particularly from private-sector customers. Demand remains supportive in power transmission and distribution, data centres, infrastructure, utilities and renewable energy.

Banks have reported healthy credit demand across corporate, small and medium enterprise and secured retail segments. Motilal Oswal expects net interest margins to recover gradually in the second half, aided by the deployment of surplus liquidity and easing funding costs, although some lenders may continue to face near-term pressure.
Metals companies expect improved performance through higher volumes, better realisations and a favourable product mix. However, rising coking coal costs in the third quarter could weigh on margins.
Consumer companies are also expecting sequential margin improvement in the second half, supported by pricing actions, cost-saving measures and operating leverage.
Cost Pressures Remain A Risk
Despite the positive outlook, the brokerage flagged input-cost pressures and geopolitical uncertainties as key risks to earnings growth.

The technology sector presents a mixed picture, with demand supported by artificial intelligence-led transformation and cost optimisation, while constrained discretionary spending and macroeconomic uncertainty continue to affect some segments.

Motilal Oswal said management commentary during the September-quarter earnings season remained constructive on demand, business expansion and execution prospects, but companies' ability to manage costs and sustain growth will remain important in the coming quarters.
